# Foundations Soil — native 26.1.2 development port
**`0.1.0-beta-port.1` · Minecraft 26.1.2 · NeoForge 26.1.2.114 · Java 25**
The full 1.21.1 `0.1.0-beta` Soil feature implementation has been migrated to native
26.1.2 APIs. **This is a compiled development port, not a validated playable modpack.**
TFC and Foundations Framework remain hard runtime dependencies. Their native
26.1.2 builds must be available and validated before gameplay testing can pass.
## Included
Persistent living-soil cells and history, physical composition and root-zone
response, solid/liquid amendments and delayed releases, Field Guide scrolling and
field editing, Soil Laboratory comparisons/trends, and integration APIs remain in
source. The port adds native saved-data codecs/namespaces, rendering/input APIs,
item/fluid definitions and transaction-based fluid containers. It does not replace
TFC's calendar, climate, hydration, crop growth or stored N/P/K.
## Build
Windows: `build_mod.bat` or the equivalent `gradlew.bat` command. A first build
requires network access. The main output is:
`build/libs/foundations_soil-26.1.2-0.1.0-beta-port.1.jar`
The sources JAR and complete source archive are development files, not mods to put
into a game's `mods` folder.
**74 native model tests pass**; three TFC-dependent tests are excluded from that
suite and await real runtime dependencies. Model tests do not start the modpack.
The 1k/10k/50k benchmarks check model/storage round trips, not live server TPS.
## Runtime dependency gate
The inspected TFC-Foundations `26.1.2` commit is
`c350b69e1300c128e3db53af947a896aa37dbca5` (candidate `0.0.0`, no playable release).
A compatible Framework native runtime was not available for this validation.
For real runtime tests, supply genuine native artifacts in `libs/` as described in
[libs/README.txt](libs/README.txt). Then use `-PmodRuntimeTests=true clean test`,
`runClient` or `runServer`. Old-version JARs are rejected, and a missing/incompatible
TFC API fails closed. No vanilla fallback, synthetic target classes or stub mods
are included. Patchouli/JEI runtime pins follow the inspected target TFC branch.
## Validation and safe testing
Read [the exact evidence and open gates](docs/ports/26.1.2/VALIDATION.md) and
[release notes](docs/ports/26.1.2/RELEASE_NOTES.md). Full game launches, actual TFC API
binding/Mixins, crop/fluids, rendering/input, multiplayer and seasonal tests remain
unexecuted. **Do not use this development build in a production world.**

Back up complete worlds. Native storage import preserves original legacy Soil
files, but this does not establish whole-world Minecraft/TFC upgrade or downgrade
compatibility. Soil payload schema/model remain 4/4; Field Ledger schema remains 5;
network protocol remains 8 within the strictly matching native platform.

## Branch and release policy

- `main`: retain Minecraft **1.21.1**, published `0.1.0-beta`.
- `mc-26.1.2`: this native development port; next playable integration target.
- `mc-26.3`: planned parallel development toward **26.4**; no Soil binary included here.

Publish each platform's own JAR and source as a GitHub Release. This port uses
`mc-26.1.2-v0.1.0-beta-port.1`, a development prerelease, never the stable/latest build.
Earlier `docs/beta/` validation records describe **1.21.1**, not native 26.x acceptance.

## Active policy
Retain **1.21.1** and target **26.1.2** for the next playable native integration.
Develop **26.3** separately toward **26.4**. The 26.3-to-26.4 transition does not
remove the retained 1.21.1 or 26.1.2 targets. Required dependencies and runtime
validation determine playable readiness; a version number change does not.
| Branch | Role |
| --- | --- |
| main | 1.21.1 retained line; 0.1.0-beta released |
| mc-26.1.2 | Native port; compiled development release with runtime gates open |
| mc-26.3 | Planned separate source port toward 26.4 |
| mc-26.4 | Start when the target release and usable dependencies are verified |
Do not silently drop required TFC/Framework dependencies or rename a legacy JAR.
Each branch pins Minecraft, NeoForge, Java and its runtime dependency versions.
Share agronomy fixes deliberately; platform APIs require separate compilation.
## Releases

Use a platform-specific tag matching the exact source version:

```
mc-1.21.1-v0.1.0-beta
mc-26.1.2-v0.1.0-beta-port.1
The first is the retained beta; the second identifies this native development port.
A `-port.N` prerelease is not a claim of completed runtime validation. Release notes
must prominently identify missing required dependencies and unexecuted game tests.
A normal playable beta/stable release requires the corresponding runtime gates.
Every actual release publishes the matching compiled JAR, sources, complete source
archive, validation notes, and checksums. Build the tagged source and check version,
Minecraft range and Java classfile level. Publish through a draft so an upload
failure cannot leave an empty public release. Never overwrite published assets;
use a new version/tag for changes. Prereleases must not become the stable/latest.
CI artifacts alone do not replace GitHub Releases. The native port pipeline also
attaches model-test and benchmark evidence, with explicit runtime limitations.
## 26.4 transition
Check official Minecraft/NeoForge release and dependency readiness before moving
the newer line. Retain earlier release tags and assets. This document is a policy,
not evidence that a background watcher exists or that 26.4 is already compatible.

# Native platform status

Retain 1.21.1, prioritize 26.1.2 playable integration, and develop 26.3 toward 26.4. The native 26.1.2 source now compiles and passes 74 model tests; actual TFC/Framework runtime, Mixin, GUI, crop and world-upgrade acceptance remains open. The roadmap below is inherited feature/history context, not proof of 26.x runtime support.

See [native validation](docs/ports/26.1.2/VALIDATION.md) for evidence and blockers. Earlier beta records below refer to 1.21.1.

# Foundations Soil 26.1.2 — 0.1.0-beta-port.1

**Compiled native development port. Not yet a playable/validated TFC modpack.**
The existing 1.21.1 beta and its GitHub release remain unchanged.

## Ported implementation

The 0.1.0-beta feature set is retained: living-soil cells, amendments, crop history,
Field Guide editing/scrolling, Soil Laboratory comparisons, physical soil and
bounded trends, API hooks, and save/network hardening.

This branch migrates that code to real Minecraft 26.1.2 / NeoForge 26.1.2.114 / Java 25:

- Identifier and native game/event APIs, screen extraction and input-event objects.
- Namespaced SavedDataType/Codec persistence and native optional NBT getters.
  Legacy Soil files can be imported without deleting or modifying the originals;
  unreadable/ambiguous data is rejected rather than overwritten.
- Native client item definitions, bucket fluid-container models, fluid model registration,
  and transaction-based fluid-container handling. Crafting ingredient format is migrated;
  TFC-specific recipe acceptance still requires the genuine native TFC implementation.
- Proper registry-created item/block property IDs and server/client network calls.
- Cached mandatory TFC API resolution and string-target required Mixins, with no
  old TFC binary or placeholder dependency on the compiler path.
- Native build/release metadata and explicit rejection of mismatched dependency JARs
  before developer runtime tests.

## Evidence

All main sources compile natively and **74 model tests pass**. Three TFC-dependent
checks are retained for the separate runtime suite, not reported as passes. The
1k/10k/50k-cell model/storage benchmark preserved every cell through compressed
save/load. GitHub CI reruns native compilation, tests and the benchmark before
publishing these artifacts. See `VALIDATION.md` and attached reports/checksums.

## Required dependencies and warning

**TFC and Foundations Framework are still hard runtime dependencies.** Their native
26.1.2 runtime compatibility has not been established. The inspected TFC-Foundations
branch is candidate 0.0.0 and has no published playable release; native Framework was
not available in this test environment. The Soil JAR cannot be used as a standalone
or vanilla replacement.

No full client/dedicated-server launch, in-game Mixin transformation, crop trial,
fluid interaction, GUI rendering, or production save migration has passed here.
This is a **development prerelease**, not a production-ready gameplay build.

Use Java 25 and Minecraft 26.1.2 only. **Back up complete worlds before testing.**
Soil's payload schema/model remain 4/4 and Field Ledger schema remains 5; the native
storage location/codec are new. Network protocol remains 8 but the game platform is
strictly different: do not mix 1.21.1 and 26.1.2 clients/servers. A file-format test
is not proof that whole Minecraft/TFC worlds can be upgraded or downgraded safely.
Restore backups rather than downgrade modified test worlds.

## Platform plan

Retain 1.21.1; prioritize playable 26.1.2 integration when its dependencies are ready;
continue the separate 26.3 line toward 26.4. Each actual platform release receives
its own tested source/JAR and GitHub tag. No 26.3/26.4 binary is implied by this release.

# Native 26.1.2 port validation — 0.1.0-beta-port.1

This is a **compiled development port**, not a validated playable modpack. The
1.21.1 beta remains separately released and is not overwritten by this branch.

## Toolchain and dependency boundary

- Minecraft **26.1.2**, NeoForge **26.1.2.114**, Java **25**, ModDevGradle **2.0.148**.
- All main/test sources compile against genuine native Minecraft/NeoForge binaries.
  No 1.21.1 Minecraft, TFC or Framework binary, fake target class or stub mod is on
  the compiler/model-test classpath.
- Runtime metadata still requires **tfc** and **foundations_framework**. A cached,
  fail-closed TFC method-handle boundary resolves genuine calendar/climate/crop
  methods during common setup. It does not simulate a fallback calendar or soil.
- Dependency checkpoint: TFC-Foundations branch `26.1.2`, commit
  `c350b69e1300c128e3db53af947a896aa37dbca5`, declares candidate `0.0.0` and has no
  published playable 26.1.2 release. Its Java/NeoForge/Patchouli/JEI pins informed
  this port. A genuine compatible Framework 26.1.2 JAR was unavailable for testing.
- Supplying legacy JARs under new filenames does not satisfy compatibility.
  Developer launch/full-runtime mode validates mod IDs and Minecraft ranges before
  invoking the real loader; loader checks and TFC API binding are still required.

## Executed local checks

**74 native model tests passed; zero failed, aborted or skipped.** Three existing
TFC-dependent tests are deliberately outside this model suite (`tfc-runtime` tag):
TFC growth/picking bytecode targets (two) and TFC-backed resource validation (one).
They are not counted as passes or disguised as successful runtime checks.

The executed suite includes:

- Native SavedDataType/Codec/SavedDataStorage write/read and save completion.
- Repeated rejection of corrupt existing data instead of creating an empty replacement.
- Explicit legacy filename import retaining the original bytes; ambiguous files rejected.
- Soil schema/model and ledger migrations, amendment queues, bounded trends and ownership.
- Packet round trips, malformed counts, replay/cooldown guards and independent scrolling.
- Native item definitions, bucket textures codec, crafting ingredients and required dependency metadata.
- Missing TFC bootstrap/read rejection: no substitute calendar is silently created.

The config fixture constructs a real minimal FML context, not a running Minecraft
server and not a replacement dependency mod. Test-only fixtures are not packaged
in the mod JAR.

## Benchmarks

`initial-native-benchmark.json` records 1k/10k/50k-cell model/storage measurements.
Every cell's saved NBT is compared after compressed serialization/deserialization.
These do **not** measure real server ticks, TFC chunk sampling, active modpacks,
network traffic, GUI rendering, or dense monitored-field memory. Heap deltas are
approximate allocations, not retained-heap measurements. Do not call them TPS data.

## Reproduce

```sh
./gradlew --no-daemon clean test build soilScaleBenchmark
```

Java 25 is required. A first Gradle build requires network access. Native CI reruns
this command and records JUnit reports and a fresh benchmark before release.

For actual native runtime validation, place genuine target-version artifacts in
`libs/TFC-Foundations-26.1.2.jar` and `libs/foundations_framework-26.1.2.jar` (or use
`-Ptfc_jar=<name>` / `-Pframework_jar=<name>`), then:

```sh
./gradlew --no-daemon -PmodRuntimeTests=true clean test
./gradlew --no-daemon runClient
./gradlew --no-daemon runServer
```

Runtime mode resolves Patchouli `26.1-94` and JEI `29.43.0.107` from the inspected
TFC target configuration. Exact successful runtime dependency versions must be
recorded before promoting this port. Missing dependencies fail explicitly.

## Open acceptance gates

| Gate | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Genuine native TFC and Framework available and compatible | Blocked / unverified |
| Full client and dedicated-server launch, `/fsoil selftest` | Not run |
| TFC method-handle binding and required Mixin transformation | Not run |
| Real planting, growth, picking, harvest, animals and amendment fluid transactions | Not run |
| TFC recipe reload, item/fluid graphics and GUI/input scale checks | Not run |
| Production multiplayer/seasonal/large-world and restart-under-load trials | Not run |
| Old complete Minecraft/TFC worlds converted safely to 26.1.2 | Not established |
| 26.3 and 26.4 native Soil binaries | Not included in this artifact |

A native compiled addon is useful port progress, but it cannot make an unfinished
required TFC port playable. Do not put this development JAR into a production world.
